review_fixes: Removed two formatting-only hunks from the engine patch, in servo-constellation/event_loop.rs and servo-constellation/process_manager.rs. They changed no behavior and do not match upstream formatting.
Widened the runner deadline test margins. A 0.3-second deadline could expire before the parent interpreter printed its start marker.

failure_triggers.content-process-failure: The blocked child calls std::process::exit(86) after a constellation acknowledgment proves that eight pending evaluations reached it.
failure_triggers.content-process-kill: The blocked child reports its process id through the barrier. After the same acknowledgment, the host runs kill -KILL on that id while the child is still blocked. The child does not exit on release in this mode, so only the signal can end it.

configuration.runner_cleanup: Every case has its own process group. The runner kills remaining group members after normal completion or a deadline.

negative_control.variation: The kill probe keeps the barrier, the process id report, and the acknowledgment, but sends no signal. All lifeline recovery remains active.
negative_control.expected_failure: Error: Content lifeline recovery failed: E4 process deadline exceeded; active=Some(DocumentIdentity { pipeline_id: (1,28), incarnation: 1 }), pending=0, calls=8
negative_control.interpretation: The child resumed and answered all eight evaluations normally, so no crash notification arrived. Recovery in the passing kill case therefore depends on the signal.

limitations: Multiprocess evidence uses unsandboxed children on macOS arm64 with software rendering.
The kill fixture uses an external SIGKILL while the child is blocked at a barrier. It does not cover a kill during JavaScript execution, during IPC writes, or during document construction.
Both process fixtures cover one affected view and an independent surviving view. Shared-process views and normal teardown races need dedicated fixtures.
Backend disconnection, failures before document construction, and remaining replacement paths remain open.
The host allocation counter is not a production registry or handle revocation mechanism.
Upstream review must settle cancellation, interruption, lifeline recovery, and callback/delegate unwind policy before integration.
No new Linux, native-input, release-performance, or remote CI evidence is claimed.
